# EVALUATION OF QUALITY IN THE LYRIC REPERTOIRE IN SPAIN: EFFECT GENERATED BY THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC

The evaluation of quality in the performing and musical arts is a complex and multidimensional challenge. Although several studies have been conducted in this regard, in this paper we focus on the lyric genre, one of the least explored manifestations. Our objective is to evaluate the quality of lyrical programming in Spain during a total of 8 seasons (2016-2024). To do so, we apply a novel methodological approach that uses Data Envelopment Analysis to estimate a synthetic indicator of quality. The aggregation process seeks to bring together the different aspects that determine quality in the scenic field, starting from the construction of five partial quality indicators, which in a second phase are synthesized into three major dimensions (technical quality, prestige and originality), and finally into a single complex indicator. The findings show that programmers adjust their strategy to maximize quality to the pressures of the environment and their own internal constraints. In addition, it has been possible to identify how the impact of the restrictions caused by the Covid-19 health crisis led to a change of trend in the repertoire management model, advocating more diverse and contemporary programs, given the lesser concern for maximizing viewership. These results are valuable as a contribution to the academic literature, but are also useful as a resource for programmers, cultural managers and public administrators to formulate cultural policies that meet audience demands, promote artistic excellence and ensure their economic sustainability
